In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • A pail is filled to 24.0 kg net and leaves the fill
  • A lid is seated (Lid_Seated)
  • The magazine runs out (Lids_Out), it is reloaded and the line carries on
  • The reader reads a label (Reader1:I.Result_Code bit 0)
  • A bad pail is pushed into Reject_Bin
  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (200 s)

Expert · par 200 s

The job

A paint line, start to finish, one pail per station. Empty 5-gallon pails come out of the hopper one at a time.

THE FILL: stop each one under the lance (PE_Fill), let the scale settle, tare it, fill white latex paint by net weight to 24.0 kg on the tank's two valves (Weight is in tenths of a kg), hold the lance in until both valves are proved shut, and keep the tank topped up from the tote.

THE LID: stop the pail under the lid press (PE_Lid) and run its sequence on its own switches — cup down with the vacuum on until Vac_OK, cup up, arm out to Arm_At_Pail, cup down, vacuum off, cup up, arm home, press down and hold, then, with the platen still down, close the four fingers on the lid's tabs (Clamp, until Clamp_Closed) and open them again (Clamp_Open) before the press goes up — then read Lid_Seated and Lid_Locked: a lid that went on cocked will not seat, and a seated lid whose tabs are not locked is a reject. Lifting with the fingers closed pulls the lid off; coming down with them closed bends the tabs. The magazine holds 8 lids: when Lids_Out comes on, flash the red lamp and wait; click the lid press to reload it.

THE LABEL: Level 4's handshake on a pail (only a pail with its lid seated gets a label).

THE CODE: the DataMan (Reader1, on EtherNet/IP) reads the code on the label as the pail passes PE_Code. The code is the paint's colour and the pail's number in it — WH0001, WH0002 … for white (RD for red, BL blue, YL yellow, GR green, BK black) — and this line runs white: the roll has a red label spliced in (RD…) and a smudged code, and both are rejects. Push off at PE_Reject anything that is not right; the good pails run off the end into Good_Bin.

The program

The program runs each station on its own flags, one pail per station. The fill: the release on Fill_Busy; the stop on the eye, the tare after 0.6 s for the scale to settle, the net weight, the two-stage fill (fast, then the dribble valve to the target), and the lance held in until Valve_Closed proves both valves shut; then the hand-on to the lid conveyor once the press is free. The lid is a step register: 0 waiting, 10 pick, 20 lift, 30 carry, 40 place, 50 let go, 60 cup up, 70 arm home, 80 press and dwell, then the fingers closed on the tabs and opened again, and 90 the check. Every output comes from the step numbers, so each one is written in one place. The label is Level 4’s handshake, only for a pail with its lid seated. The code is the DataMan’s trigger and results handshakes, the string’s first two letters taken with MID and compared with WH. One reject flag per pail, which the lid, the label and the code can each set, fires the pusher at PE_Reject; and the lamps.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

The rungs

Watch for

Lifting the press with the fingers still closed pulls the lid off; bringing it down with them closed bends the tabs out of reach. The fingers belong to the dwell at the bottom of the stroke, closed and opened again while the platen is down.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: Start seals Run in; Stop or a tripped E-stop breaks it

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Line running) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: the run lamp
rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: THE TANK kept topped up from the tote: open under 85 %, sealed in to 90 %, and the high-level switch shuts it whatever the transmitter says

pred.q: Refill is on, Tank_High is on and Tank_Level is 86. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Refill is off. It stops at XIO(Tank_High).

rungs.words: When either (Tank_Level (Tank: level, %) is less than 85) or (Refill (Tank: refill valve from the paint tote) is on), Tank_Level is less than 90 and Tank_High (Tank: high-level switch) is off, the rung turns Refill on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Tank_Level,85) Less Than asks: true when Tank_Level is less than 85.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Refill) Examine If Closed asks: true when Refill is on.
  2. LES(Tank_Level,90) Less Than asks: true when Tank_Level is less than 90.
  3. XIO(Tank_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Tank_High is off.
  4. OTE(Refill) Output Energize does: turns Refill on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Refill on, and Refill’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE FILL. RELEASE one empty pail when the fill station is free
rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on, Pail_Ready (Hopper: an empty pail waits at the gate) is on, Fill_Busy (A pail is on its way to or at the fill) is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Pail_Release (Hopper: release one pail (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and latches Fill_Busy on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Pail_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pail_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Fill_Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Busy is off.
  4. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Pail_Release) Output Energize does: turns Pail_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Fill_Busy) Output Latch does: latches Fill_Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fill_Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: the eye at the lance stops it, centred under it

pred.q: PE_Fill is on and Fill_Done is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: At_Fill latches on.

rungs.words: When PE_Fill (Pail centred under the fill lance) is on and Fill_Done (The pail is full) is off, the rung latches At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Fill is on.
  2. XIO(Fill_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Done is off.
  3. OTL(At_Fill) Output Latch does: latches At_Fill on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: At_Fill stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: the infeed runs until a pail is at the fill
rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on and At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) is off, the rung turns In_Conv_Run (Infeed conveyor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(At_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when At_Fill is off.
  3. OTE(In_Conv_Run) Output Energize does: turns In_Conv_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: the scale conveyor carries it on once it is full, the lance is out of it and the lid press is free

pred.q: Run is on, At_Fill is on, Fill_Done is off, Lance_Up is on and Lid_Busy is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Scale_Run is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on and either (At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) is off) or (Fill_Done (The pail is full) is on, Lance_Up (Tank: lance up (switch)) is on and Lid_Busy (A pail is on the lid conveyor) is off), the rung turns Scale_Run (Weighing conveyor under the fill) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(At_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when At_Fill is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Fill_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Done is on.
    2. XIC(Lance_Up) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lance_Up is on.
    3. XIO(Lid_Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Lid_Busy is off.
  3. OTE(Scale_Run) Output Energize does: turns Scale_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: TARE: the pail stops, the scale settles…
rungs.words: When At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) is on, the rung runs the timer T_Settle (The scale settles before the tare) toward 600 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
  2. TON(T_Settle,600,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Settle toward 600 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Settle counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: …and the empty pail is weighed once

pred.q: T_Settle.DN is on and Tare_Taken is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Tare is written and Tare_Taken latches on.

rungs.words: When T_Settle.DN (the done bit of T_Settle: The scale settles before the tare) is on and Tare_Taken (The empty pail has been weighed) is off, the rung puts Weight (Scale: gross weight, tenths of a kg) into Tare (The empty pail, tenths of a kg) and latches Tare_Taken on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Settle.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Settle.DN is on.
  2. XIO(Tare_Taken) Examine If Open asks: true when Tare_Taken is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Weight,Tare) Move does: puts Weight into Tare. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Tare_Taken) Output Latch does: latches Tare_Taken on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Tare_Taken stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: NET: what has gone in
rungs.words: When Tare_Taken (The empty pail has been weighed) is on, the rung makes Net (What has gone in, tenths of a kg) = Weight (Scale: gross weight, tenths of a kg) − Tare (The empty pail, tenths of a kg).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  2. SUB(Weight,Tare,Net) Subtract does: makes Net = Weight − Tare. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: FILL while the pail is weighed and not full

pred.q: Run is on, At_Fill is off, Tare_Taken is on and Fill_Done is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fill_Go is off. It stops at XIC(At_Fill).

rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on, At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) is on, Tare_Taken (The empty pail has been weighed) is on and Fill_Done (The pail is full) is off, the rung turns Fill_Go (Filling) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
  3. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
  4. XIO(Fill_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Done is off.
  5. OTE(Fill_Go) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Go on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: the lance goes in and stays in until both valves are proved shut, so the last of the paint goes into the pail
rungs.words: When either (Fill_Go (Filling) is on) or (At_Fill (A pail is stopped under the lance) is on, Tare_Taken (The empty pail has been weighed) is on and Valve_Closed (Tank: both valves proved shut) is off), the rung turns Lance_Down (Tank: the fill lance down into the pail) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(At_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_Fill is on.
    2. XIC(Tare_Taken) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tare_Taken is on.
    3. XIO(Valve_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Valve_Closed is off.
  2. OTE(Lance_Down) Output Energize does: turns Lance_Down on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: …and has been in long enough

pred.q: Fill_Go is on and Lance_Up is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: T_LanceIn times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Fill_Go (Filling) is on and Lance_Up (Tank: lance up (switch)) is off, the rung runs the timer T_LanceIn (The lance is in before the valves open) toward 800 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIO(Lance_Up) Examine If Open asks: true when Lance_Up is off.
  3. TON(T_LanceIn,800,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_LanceIn toward 800 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_LanceIn counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: THE BULK: the butterfly to 22.0 kg (the target, 24.0 kg, less 2.0 on the dribble)
rungs.words: When Fill_Go (Filling) is on, T_LanceIn.DN (the done bit of T_LanceIn: The lance is in before the valves open) is on and Net (What has gone in, tenths of a kg) is less than 220, the rung turns Fill_Fast (Tank: the bulk (butterfly) valve) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fill_Go) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fill_Go is on.
  2. XIC(T_LanceIn.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_LanceIn.DN is on.
  3. LES(Net,220) Less Than asks: true when Net is less than 220.
  4. OTE(Fill_Fast) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Fast on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: THE DRIBBLE to 23.8 kg: the last 0.2 kg is in the air when it shuts

pred.q: Fill_Go is off, T_LanceIn.DN is off and Net is 238. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fill_Slow is off. It stops at XIC(Fill_Go).

  4. EQU(Lid_Step,0) Equal asks: true when Lid_Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.

rungs.head: Rung 39
rungs.comment: HANDED ON to the outfeed, a bad lid marked for the reject
rungs.words: When Lid_Done (The lid press is done with the pail) is on and PE_Lid (Pail centred under the lid press) is off, each path is tested on its own: it unlatches Lid_Done; it unlatches At_Lid (A pail is stopped under the lid press); it unlatches Lid_Busy (A pail is on the lid conveyor); it latches Out_Busy (A pail is on the outfeed) on; if Lid_Bad (The lid did not seat) is on, it latches Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected) on; it unlatches Lid_Bad.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Lid_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lid_Done is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Lid) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Lid is off.
  3. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Lid_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lid_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(At_Lid) Output Unlatch does: unlatches At_Lid. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Lid_Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lid_Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Out_Busy) Output Latch does: latches Out_Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 5
    1. XIC(Lid_Bad) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lid_Bad is on.
    2. OTL(Rej_Flag) Output Latch does: latches Rej_Flag on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Lid_Bad) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lid_Bad. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Out_Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 40
rungs.comment: THE LABEL. The outfeed runs unless a pail is held at the labeler

pred.q: Run is on and Hold is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Out_Conv_Run is on.

rungs.words: When Run (Line running) is on and Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler) is off, the rung turns Out_Conv_Run (Outfeed: labeler, code reader, reject) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when Hold is off.
  3. OTE(Out_Conv_Run) Output Energize does: turns Out_Conv_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 41
rungs.comment: a pail with its lid seated is held under the roller (a rejected one goes past unlabeled)
rungs.words: When PE_Label (Pail at the labeler's roller) is on, Lbl_Done (The labeler has had its turn at the pail) is off and Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected) is off, the rung latches Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Label) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Label is on.
  2. XIO(Lbl_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Lbl_Done is off.
  3. XIO(Rej_Flag) Examine If Open asks: true when Rej_Flag is off.
  4. OTL(Hold) Output Latch does: latches Hold on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Hold stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 42
rungs.comment: it settles

pred.q: Hold is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Dwell is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(Hold).

rungs.words: When Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler) is on, the rung runs the timer Dwell (The pail settles at the labeler) toward 300 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. TON(Dwell,300,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Dwell toward 300 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Dwell counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 43
rungs.comment: APPLY when the labeler is ready (no roll, no Ready: the pail waits for a new roll)
rungs.words: When Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler) is on, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: The pail settles at the labeler) is on, Lbl_Ready (Labeler: ready) is on and Lbl_Done (The labeler has had its turn at the pail) is off, the rung latches Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in (hold until PadIn)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  3. XIC(Lbl_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_Ready is on.
  4. XIO(Lbl_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Lbl_Done is off.
  5. OTL(Apply) Output Latch does: latches Apply on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Apply stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 44
rungs.comment: the roller back at the end of its stroke

pred.q: Lbl_PadIn is on and Lbl_Error is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Apply is unlatched.

rungs.words: When either (Lbl_PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke) is on) or (Lbl_Error (Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label) is on), the rung unlatches Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in (hold until PadIn)).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Lbl_PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_PadIn is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lbl_Error) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_Error is on.
  2. OTU(Apply) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Apply. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Apply when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 45
rungs.comment: done: a pail that came away without its label is marked for the reject
rungs.words: When Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler) is on and Lbl_PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke) is on, each path is tested on its own: it latches Lbl_Done (The labeler has had its turn at the pail) on; if Lbl_Labeled (Labeler: the pail under the roller carries a label) is off, it latches Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. XIC(Lbl_PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_PadIn is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Lbl_Done) Output Latch does: latches Lbl_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Lbl_Labeled) Examine If Open asks: true when Lbl_Labeled is off.
    2. OTL(Rej_Flag) Output Latch does: latches Rej_Flag on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Lbl_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 46
rungs.comment: let it go

pred.q: Lbl_Done is off, Apply is on and Lbl_PadIn is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Hold is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Lbl_Done).

rungs.words: When Lbl_Done (The labeler has had its turn at the pail) is on, Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in (hold until PadIn)) is off and Lbl_PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke) is off, the rung unlatches Hold (The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Lbl_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_Done is on.
  2. XIO(Apply) Examine If Open asks: true when Apply is off.
  3. XIO(Lbl_PadIn) Examine If Open asks: true when Lbl_PadIn is off.
  4. OTU(Hold) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Hold. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Hold when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 47
rungs.comment: THE CODE. Triggers allowed
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung turns Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr: 1. OTE(Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 48
rungs.comment: the eye at the reader triggers it as the pail goes by…
rungs.words: When PE_Code (Pail at the code reader) is on, this is the first scan of it and Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Reader1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Code) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Code is on.
  2. ONS(Code_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Code_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. XIC(Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. OTL(Reader1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Reader1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Reader1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 49
rungs.comment: …and the trigger drops on its acknowledge
rungs.words: When Reader1:O.Trigger is on and Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Reader1:O.Trigger.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reader1:O.Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:O.Trigger is on.
  2. XIC(Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  3. OTU(Reader1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reader1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Reader1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 50
rungs.comment: THE RESULT: the code and the string, then acknowledge
rungs.words: When Reader1:I.Results_Available is on and Reader1:O.Results_Ack is off, the rung puts Reader1:I.Result_Code into Code_Result (The reader's result code), copies 64 elements from Reader1:I.Result_Data[0] to Code_Text (The string the reader decoded), latches Code_Seen (The reader has answered for this pail) on and latches Reader1:O.Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reader1:I.Results_Available) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Results_Available is on.
  2. XIO(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Reader1:O.Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Reader1:I.Result_Code,Code_Result) Move does: puts Reader1:I.Result_Code into Code_Result. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. COP(Reader1:I.Result_Data[0],Code_Text,64) Copy File does: copies 64 elements from Reader1:I.Result_Data[0] to Code_Text.
    Path 3
    1. OTL(Code_Seen) Output Latch does: latches Code_Seen on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Reader1:O.Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Code_Seen stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 51
rungs.comment: the code is the paint's colour and the pail's number, WH0001, WH0002 …: its first two letters are the colour
rungs.words: When Code_Seen (The reader has answered for this pail) is on, the rung takes 2 characters of Code_Text (The string the reader decoded) from position 1 into Code_Color (Its first two letters: the paint colour).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Code_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Code_Seen is on.
  2. MID(Code_Text,2,1,Code_Color) Middle String does: takes 2 characters of Code_Text from position 1 into Code_Color.

rungs.head: Rung 52
rungs.comment: no read, or a label of another colour (a red one spliced into the roll): reject

pred.q: Code_Seen is on, Code_Result.0 is off, Code_Color is 23 and 'WH' is 22. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Rej_Flag latches on.

rungs.words: When Code_Seen (The reader has answered for this pail) is on and either (Code_Result.0 (The reader's result code) is off) or (Code_Color (Its first two letters: the paint colour) is not 'WH'), the rung latches Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Code_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Code_Seen is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Code_Result.0) Examine If Open asks: true when Code_Result.0 is off.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(Code_Color,'WH') Not Equal asks: true when Code_Color is not 'WH'.
  3. OTL(Rej_Flag) Output Latch does: latches Rej_Flag on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Rej_Flag stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 53
rungs.comment: the acknowledge drops once the reader has cleared Results_Available
rungs.words: When Reader1:I.Results_Available is off, the rung unlatches Reader1:O.Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Reader1:I.Results_Available) Examine If Open asks: true when Reader1:I.Results_Available is off.
  2. OTU(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reader1:O.Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Reader1:O.Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 54
rungs.comment: THE REJECT. At the pusher's eye a marked pail is pushed off…
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Pail at the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: it latches Rej_Seen (The pail has reached the reject eye) on; if Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected) is on, it latches Fire (Push this pail off) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Rej_Seen) Output Latch does: latches Rej_Seen on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Rej_Flag) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rej_Flag is on.
    2. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Rej_Seen stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 55
rungs.comment: …the pusher stays out until the pail has left the eye: it is caught a pail-width ahead of the paddle, so the stroke has time to meet it
rungs.words: When Fire (Push this pail off) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  2. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 56
rungs.comment: once it has gone by (or off), count it and free the outfeed for the next

pred.q: Rej_Seen is on, PE_Reject is on and Fire is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Reject_Count is not written (it keeps its value), Good_Count is not written (it keeps its value), Fire is left as it was, Rej_Seen is left as it was, Rej_Flag is left as it was, Lbl_Done is left as it was, Code_Seen is left as it was and Out_Busy is left as it was. It stops at XIO(PE_Reject).

rungs.words: When Rej_Seen (The pail has reached the reject eye) is on and PE_Reject (Pail at the reject pusher) is off, each path is tested on its own: if Fire (Push this pail off) is on, it makes Reject_Count (Shown on the toolbar: pails rejected) = Reject_Count + 1; if Fire is off, it makes Good_Count (Shown on the toolbar: good pails out) = Good_Count + 1; it unlatches Fire; it unlatches Rej_Seen; it unlatches Rej_Flag (The pail on the outfeed is to be rejected); it unlatches Lbl_Done (The labeler has had its turn at the pail); it unlatches Code_Seen (The reader has answered for this pail); it unlatches Out_Busy (A pail is on the outfeed).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Rej_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rej_Seen is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  3. A branch of 8 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
    2. ADD(Reject_Count,1,Reject_Count) Add does: makes Reject_Count = Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fire) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire is off.
    2. ADD(Good_Count,1,Good_Count) Add does: makes Good_Count = Good_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Rej_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Rej_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Rej_Flag) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Rej_Flag. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Lbl_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lbl_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Code_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Code_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. OTU(Out_Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Out_Busy. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 57
rungs.words: When Fl_Bit (Flasher) is off, the rung runs the timer T_Flash (Flasher) toward 500 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Fl_Bit) Examine If Open asks: true when Fl_Bit is off.
  2. TON(T_Flash,500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Flash toward 500 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Flash counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 58
rungs.comment: a half-second flasher

pred.q: T_Flash.DN is on and Fl_Bit is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Fl_Bit is left as it was and Fl_Bit latches on.

rungs.words: When T_Flash.DN (the done bit of T_Flash: Flasher) is on, each path is tested on its own: if Fl_Bit (Flasher) is on, it unlatches Fl_Bit; if Fl_Bit is off, it latches Fl_Bit on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Flash.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Flash.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
    2. OTU(Fl_Bit) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fl_Bit. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fl_Bit) Examine If Open asks: true when Fl_Bit is off.
    2. OTL(Fl_Bit) Output Latch does: latches Fl_Bit on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fl_Bit stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 59
rungs.comment: THE LAMPS: lids or labels low
rungs.words: When either (Lids_Low (Lid press: magazine low) is on) or (Lbl_Low (Labeler: labels low) is on), the rung turns Lamp_Amber (Amber lamp: lids or labels low) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Lids_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lids_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lbl_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_Low is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 60
rungs.comment: out: the red lamp flashes. Click the lid press to reload its magazine, the labeler for a new roll

pred.q: Lids_Out is on, Lbl_Error is off and Fl_Bit is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Red is off. It stops at XIC(Fl_Bit).

rungs.words: When either (Lids_Out (Lid press: magazine empty) is on) or (Lbl_Error (Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label) is on) and Fl_Bit (Flasher) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Red (Red lamp: lids or labels out: reload) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Lids_Out) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lids_Out is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lbl_Error) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lbl_Error is on.
  2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Red) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Red on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Hold.desc: The outfeed is held with a pail at the labeler

Lbl_Done.desc: The labeler has had its turn at the pail

Dwell.desc: The pail settles at the labeler

Apply.desc: Labeler: drive the roller in (hold until PadIn)

Lbl_PadIn.desc: Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke

Lbl_Error.desc: Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label

Lbl_Labeled.desc: Labeler: the pail under the roller carries a label

Code_ONS.desc: One-shot at the code reader's eye

Code_Seen.desc: The reader has answered for this pail

Code_Color.desc: Its first two letters: the paint colour

Rej_Seen.desc: The pail has reached the reject eye

Reject_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: pails rejected

Good_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: good pails out

Lamp_Amber.desc: Amber lamp: lids or labels low

Lamp_Red.desc: Red lamp: lids or labels out: reload
